headline: GOLD HEADS FOR 4% WEEKLY WIPEOUT AS FED RATE CUT HOPES DIE ON CPI SHOCK
snippet: Gold fell to $4,530 Friday — down 4% on the week and 18% below its January all-time high of $5,589 — after April CPI surged to 3.8% year-over-year, its hottest reading since May 2023. The inflation shock forced markets to reprice the Fed from rate cuts to possible rate hikes, lifting the dollar and crushing precious metals across the board.

headline: TRUMP FLIES HOME FROM BEIJING EMPTY-HANDED: NO RARE EARTH DEAL, HEAVY ELEMENTS STILL DOWN 50%
snippet: President Trump left Beijing on Friday calling the visit a 'success' but without any binding rare earth agreement — US imports of dysprosium, terbium, and yttrium remain roughly 50% below levels seen before China's April 2025 export controls. Talks centered on extending the existing one-year trade truce before it expires this fall, but no formal deal was announced, leaving Western defence and tech supply chains still exposed.

headline: WHY 3.8% INFLATION SENT SILVER DOWN 10%, NOT UP: THE MECHANISM NOBODY EXPLAINS
snippet: Silver plunged 10.6% to $77.52 in a single session on May 15 — far outpacing gold's 1.8% drop — because hot inflation forces traders to reprice the Fed toward rate hikes rather than cuts, lifting the dollar and crushing metals. CME FedWatch now assigns near-zero probability to any 2026 rate cut; silver's industrial exposure to China trade made the move even more violent.

headline: $18.5 BILLION GOLD GIANT BORN: EQUINOX SWALLOWS ORLA IN ALL-STOCK MERGER
snippet: Equinox Gold (TSX: EQX) and Orla Mining (TSX: OLA) agreed on May 13 to combine in an at-market all-stock deal that creates an $18.5 billion North American senior gold producer with 1.1 million ounces of annual production from six operating mines across Canada, the US, Mexico, and Nicaragua. Orla shareholders receive 1.0 Equinox share per share held; the combined entity will become Canada's second-largest domestic gold producer, targeting completion in Q3 2026.

headline: NGEX MINERALS HITS 1,740 G/T GOLD OVER 2 METRES INSIDE A 207 G/T BROADER ZONE IN ARGENTINA
snippet: NGEx Minerals (TSX-V: NGEX) released final Phase 4 drill results from its Lunahuasi copper-gold-silver project in Argentina's San Juan province, headlined by a 2-metre interval grading an extraordinary 1,740 g/t gold within a broader 17.3-metre zone averaging 207.79 g/t gold. The completed Phase 4 programme covered 27,318 metres across 32 holes; Phase 5 is targeted for Q4 2026, with a new high-grade zone also confirmed 300 metres east of the main Mars zone.

headline: BARRICK Q1 SHOCKER: 719,000 OZ GOLD, REVENUE UP 67%, $3B BUYBACK, NORTH AMERICAN IPO AHEAD
snippet: Barrick Mining (NYSE: B) reported Q1 2026 gold output of 719,000 ounces — beating the top end of its 640,000–680,000 oz guidance range — with revenue rising 67% to $5.22 billion, operating cash flow up 111% to $2.55 billion, and EPS of $0.98, up 256% year-over-year. The board approved a $3 billion share buyback and flagged a forthcoming North American IPO of its gold assets, signalling confidence in sustained high gold prices.

headline: COPPER DROPS 5% FROM ALL-TIME HIGH AS JUNE 30 U.S. TARIFF DECISION DAY DRAWS NEAR
snippet: Copper fell to $6.23/lb on May 15, its sharpest single-day decline in weeks, as traders locked in gains after a record rally while awaiting a critical June 30 U.S. government deadline on phased tariffs for refined copper imports. The structural supply deficit story remains intact — analysts project a 600,000-tonne shortfall in 2026 — but near-term headwinds from China demand softness and profit-taking are outweighing that thesis for now.

headline: PREMIER AMERICAN URANIUM SPUDS 100,000-FT ISR DRILL CAMPAIGN IN WYOMING'S POWDER RIVER BASIN
snippet: Premier American Uranium (TSX-V: PUR) commenced a 100,000-foot ISR exploration drill programme at its Kaycee project in Wyoming on May 14, targeting infill and step-out holes across 110 miles of identified roll-front uranium mineralisation on 29,841 acres in the Powder River Basin. The programme aims to build toward a mineral resource estimate, following positive results from 2025 and a separate metallurgical drilling start at the company's Cebolleta project in New Mexico.

headline: NDPR FELL 21% IN APRIL BUT SITS 88% ABOVE JANUARY OPEN — CHINA'S JUNE QUOTA RELEASE IS THE PIVOT
snippet: NdPr oxide retreated sharply in April to $99.61/kg after a powerful Q1 rally but remains 88% above its January open and above the cost base of major Western producers MP Materials and Lynas. The market-defining event to watch is China's mid-year MIIT mining quota announcement, expected in June, which will signal whether second-half supply tightens or eases — the outcome likely determining whether NdPr reclaims $120 or slides back toward $80.

headline: LITHIUM CARBONATE UP 78% IN WEEKS: CHINA'S VAT REBATE CUT DETONATED A GLOBAL BATTERY SUPPLY FRENZY
snippet: Lithium carbonate in China surged 78% in just over a month after Beijing's removal of VAT export rebates on lithium-ion batteries from April 2026 prompted battery-makers to front-load overseas shipments, driving carbonate to its highest price since late 2023 before an easing. Regulatory uncertainty in Yichun and the prolonged suspension of CATL's Jianxiawo mine keep supply constrained, with non-Chinese lithium producers — including Albemarle and Lithium Americas — seen as structural beneficiaries.

headline: GOLD STOCKS PRIMED TO OUTPERFORM BULLION FOR THE FIRST TIME IN YEARS — HERE'S THE CASE
snippet: With gold-miner valuations still lagging the metal's 2024–2025 bull run, analysts argue the conditions for a long-awaited re-rating are now in place: record free-cash-flow margins, a wave of M&A consolidation, and sector undervaluation versus historical multiples. Barrick's Q1 free cash flow surging 195% and the Equinox-Orla mega-merger are cited as leading indicators that the structural shift is already underway.

headline: THE U.S. CRITICAL MINERALS PROBLEM ISN'T MINING — IT'S DECADES OF MISSING PROCESSING EXPERTISE
snippet: Despite record investment in domestic critical mineral mines, the US still lacks the metallurgical expertise and refining facilities to turn ore into usable rare earths and battery metals — a gap China spent three decades deliberately building and cannot be closed quickly. The analysis argues that opening more mines without processing capacity simply shifts the bottleneck one step earlier in the supply chain, and that training a skilled workforce and building refineries takes far longer than a mine permit.
